{{for|persons of a similar name|Elizabeth Kelly (disambiguation)}}
'''Elizabeth J. Kelly''' is an American statistician who works at the [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]] on statistical problems in [[environmental assessment]], [[environmental remediation]], and [[plutonium]] storage and disposal.{{r|highlights}}

==Education and career==
Kelly majored in mathematics at the [[University of Southern California]], graduating in 1965. She stayed at the University of Southern California for a master's degree in mathematics, earned in 1967,{{r|profile}} completed a Ph.D. in [[biostatistics]] at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] in 1984,{{r|profile|ucla}} and joined the Los Alamos National Laboratory research staff in 1985.{{r|highlights}}

==Recognition==
In 2016, Kelly was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]] (ASA),{{r|highlights}} associated with the ASA Section on Statistics in Defense and National Security.{{r|sdns}} She is a 2020 winner of the ASA Statistics in Physical Engineering Sciences Award, shared with two other Los Alamos statisticians, Kirk Veirs and Brian Weaver.{{r|spes}}
